guard-phpのスキルからsetupを削除し、guardスキルにしてください。これはCLIの使い方を説明するスキルでありAgents Skillsのプラクティスを調査、それに則り簡潔に記載が必要です。
skillsにreferencesを持たせユースケースやGitHub Actionsでの使い方などはそちらで記載しSKILL.mdから参照を入れてください。
guard-phpを確認し、setupの記述を外してCLIの使い方を中心としたguardスキルに整理します。skill-creatorスキルを使い、Agent Skillsの公式プラクティスを調べたうえで、ユースケースやGitHub Actionsの説明をreferencesへ分けます。

既存のguardスキルに加え、metrics・structure・documentation用のsetupスキルが3つありました。これらをguardへ統合し、SKILL.mdには基本操作と参照先を残します。公式仕様でも、詳細を必要なときだけ読むreferencesへの分離が推奨されています。[Agent Skills仕様](https://agentskills.io/specification)

GitHub Actionsの例はfind-docsスキルで現行の使い方を確認し、Guardのコマンドはローカルの実装・ヘルプと照合します。
CLIの現行仕様を確認しました。フィルターは表示だけを絞るため、隠れたエラーでも終了コードは1になります。また、baselineの再生成は新しい違反も記録します。こうした操作上の注意をCLIリファレンスへまとめ、旧setupスキルへの案内もguardへ更新します。

+---
+name: guard
+description: >-

+  guard commands, rule inspection, findings, configuration repairs, baselines,

+
+# Guard
+
+Run the installed CLI from the target project's root. Read its `guard.yaml` and
+existing Composer command to identify the policy and paths in use. Use the
+project's `composer guard` script for its usual check; invoke the CLI directly
+when selecting commands or options:
+
+```bash
+vendor/bin/guard --help
+vendor/bin/guard rules
+vendor/bin/guard check
+```
+
+## Command rules
+
+- `--config=FILE` selects a policy relative to the working directory. Project
+  paths and baseline paths resolve relative to that policy's directory.
+- Use `--format=ai` for compact diagnostics or `--format=json` for parsing.
+  `--query`, `--fixable`, and `--level` on `check` filter display only; hidden
+  errors still fail the command.

+  within the requested scope. Built-in repairs change configuration fields;
+  metrics, directory structure, and Markdown findings need manual edits.

+# Guard CLI
+
+Invoke `vendor/bin/guard COMMAND` from the project root. No command means `check`.
+Use `guard COMMAND --help` to confirm the installed version's options.
+
+## Commands
+
+| Command | Behavior |
+|---------|----------|
+| `rules` | List effective rules after imports and overrides, without reading target files. |
+| `check` | Report violations without modifying files. |
+| `fix --dry-run` | Show proposed configuration diffs without writing them. |
+| `fix` | Apply supported repairs, then report remaining violations. |
+| `baseline` | Write all current violations to a baseline; leave source and configuration files unchanged. |
+| `init` | Create a policy from detected presets and legacy policies; refuse to overwrite an existing policy. |
+
+## Options
+
+| Applies to | Option | Meaning |
+|------------|--------|---------|
+| All policy commands | `-c`, `--config=FILE` | Policy path relative to the working directory; default `guard.yaml`. |
+| `rules`, `check`, `fix`, `baseline` | `--format=text\|human\|ai\|json` | Default `ai` in detected agent sessions, otherwise `text`; `human` aliases `text`. |
+| `rules`, `check` | `--query=TEXT` | Case-insensitive literal search across rule IDs, paths, messages, levels, and fixability. |
+| `check` | `--fixable` | Display only findings with automatic repair support. |
+| `check` | `--level=error\|warning` | Display one severity. |
+| `check` | `--baseline=FILE` | Baseline relative to the policy directory; default `guard-baseline.json` there, if present. |
+| `check` | `--no-baseline` | Disable suppression; incompatible with `--baseline`. |
+| `baseline` | `-o`, `--output=FILE` | Baseline destination relative to the policy directory; default `guard-baseline.json`. Parent directory must exist. |
+| `init` | `--import=NAMES` | Comma-separated or repeated preset names; replaces automatic detection. |
+
+Check filters combine with AND and affect only displayed findings. Baseline
+suppression happens first. Neither filters nor baselines limit `fix`.
+
+## Reports and exit codes
+
+| Code | Meaning |
+|------|---------|
+| `0` | No active required violation; warnings may remain. `rules`, `init`, and `baseline` completed successfully. |
+| `1` | Active required violations remain, including ones hidden by display filters. |
+| `2` | Invalid command, policy, input document, baseline, or extension. Read stderr's `Guard error:` message. |
+
+`baseline` exits `0` after writing successfully even when it recorded violations.
+`fix --dry-run` reports whether the planned result would pass; exit `0` does not
+mean the files already comply.
+
+`rules --format=json` returns `rules` and `count`. Each rule includes `id`,
+`target`, `level`, `fixable`, `message`, and resolved `details`.
+
+Check and fix JSON includes `findings`, `changes`, `diffs`, `action`, `success`,
+and `summary`. Findings contain `path`, `rule`, `level`, `message`, and `fixable`.
+`summary` counts displayed findings; when filtering or a baseline is active,
+use `totalSummary` and `selection` to account for hidden active findings, and
+`baseline` for suppression counts. `success: false` corresponds to exit `1`.
+Errors with exit `2` are stderr diagnostics, so check the exit code before
+parsing stdout as JSON.
+
+`action` is `checked`, `changed`, `would change`, or `blocked`. Proposed diffs
+with `blocked` are not applied. `changes` uses absolute paths; finding and diff
+paths are relative to the policy directory.
+
+For an unexpected missing finding, inspect the selected policy, automatic
+baseline, display filters, and `collect` scope. For exit `2`, correct the named
+input before rerunning; it is not a policy violation to suppress.

+# Guard use cases
+
+## Inspect and resolve findings
+
+```bash
+vendor/bin/guard rules --query=phpstan --format=ai
+vendor/bin/guard check --query=phpstan --format=json
+vendor/bin/guard check --fixable
+vendor/bin/guard check --level=warning
+```
+
+`rules` explains configured expectations even for compliant or missing files.
+Use `check` to inspect actual findings. An empty filtered report can still exit
+`1`; finish with an unfiltered check.
+
+For configuration repairs:
+
+```bash
+vendor/bin/guard fix --dry-run
+vendor/bin/guard fix
+vendor/bin/guard check
+```
+
+Review all proposed files: `fix` has no query filter and includes baselined
+violations. An unsatisfied required configuration rule blocks the planned
+writes. Resolve missing files, conflicting assertions, and manual fields before
+retrying. Source, structure, and Markdown findings require manual changes and
+do not block configuration repairs.
+
+## Record existing violations
+
+Use a baseline when the task calls for accepting existing findings while
+detecting new ones:
+
+```bash
+vendor/bin/guard baseline
+vendor/bin/guard check
+vendor/bin/guard check --no-baseline
+```
+
+Review and commit `guard-baseline.json` with the policy. Entries match exact
+paths, rule IDs, severity, messages, and occurrence counts. Changed metric
+values, including improvements still above a limit, produce new findings.
+
+To refresh after fixing findings, inspect `check --no-baseline` first, then
+regenerate and review the diff. Regeneration records all current violations,
+including new ones. Stale entries are reported as `unmatched` without failing.
+Choose a location allowed by the project's structure policy. For an existing
+`baselines/` directory:
+
+```bash
+vendor/bin/guard baseline --output=baselines/guard.json
+vendor/bin/guard check --baseline=baselines/guard.json
+```
+
+## Create or inspect a policy
+
+When a new policy is requested and none exists:
+
+```bash
+vendor/bin/guard init
+```
+
+`init` detects tool presets, production roots, and README headings, and migrates
+`loc.yaml`, `tree.yaml`, and `doc-guard.yaml` settings when present. If no root
+`docs/` directory exists, detection includes `disable-doc`, which forbids creating
+that directory. Review the generated imports and declarations before using them.
+
+To select only named presets instead of detection:
+
+```bash
+vendor/bin/guard init --import=metrics,structure
+```
+
+For an existing policy, edit within the requested scope and use `guard rules`
+and `guard check` to verify it. Imports are relative to the file declaring them;
+target paths are relative to the main policy. Later imports and project values
+override earlier values while retaining unspecified fields.
+
+`collect` applies to every policy. When present, it replaces section reading
+scopes such as `metrics.source` and `structure.paths`; metrics then read every
+PHP file in that collection. Declared documents and configuration files outside
+it are silently skipped, including missing ones. Inspect it when expected
+findings disappear. See the [policy schema](https://github.com/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/blob/main/packages/guard-php/docs/configuration.md)
+for merge rules and scope syntax.
+
+## Composer and monorepos
+
+When adding a reusable command is requested, merge this into existing Composer
+scripts and retain other gates:
+
+```json
+{
+  "scripts": {"guard": "guard check"},
+  "scripts-descriptions": {"guard": "Check project policies with Guard."}
+}
+```
+
+Include `@guard` in `lint` when it is a project gate. In a monorepo, use the owning
+package's command, or select its policy explicitly from the repository root:
+
+```bash
+composer --working-dir=packages/example guard
+vendor/bin/guard check --config=packages/example/guard.yaml
+```
+
+The second form assumes Guard is installed at the repository root. `--config`
+selects the policy and base for target paths; it does not change the executable.

+# Guard in GitHub Actions
+
+Add Guard to the existing lint job after installing Composer dependencies,
+including the dev dependency `k-kinzal/guard-php`. Use a PHP version and extensions
+compatible with the project's locked dependencies. A job that already runs
+`composer lint` with `@guard` does not need another Guard step.
+
+```yaml
+- name: Check project policies
+  run: vendor/bin/guard check --format=text
+```
+
+CI checks the committed `guard.yaml` and baseline. Run `init`, `fix`, and baseline
+generation locally when requested, review their changes, and commit the result.
+Keep Guard's nonzero exit status so violations and invalid inputs fail the job.
+
+## Standalone workflow
+
+This example assumes a root Composer project with a committed lock file, Guard
+installed as a dev dependency, and a reviewed `guard.yaml`. Adapt `main`, PHP
+`8.5`, and extensions to the target project. Keep action pins consistent with
+the repository's update policy.
+
+```yaml
+name: Guard
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash
+
+jobs:
+  guard:
+    name: Check project policies
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
+      - name: Set up PHP
+        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
+        with:
+          php-version: '8.5'
+          extensions: dom
+          coverage: none
+          tools: composer:v2
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: composer install --no-interaction --prefer-dist --no-progress
+      - name: Check project policies
+        run: vendor/bin/guard check --format=text
+```
+
+## Package policies and reports
+
+For a package with its own dependencies, set `working-directory` on both the
+install and check steps, or on the job's `defaults.run`. For a root installation
+checking a package policy:
+
+```yaml
+- name: Check package policies
+  run: vendor/bin/guard check --config=packages/example/guard.yaml --format=text
+```
+
+For a JSON report in an existing job, use a permitted output directory such as
+`build/` and Bash `pipefail` to retain Guard's exit status through `tee`:
+
+```yaml
+- name: Check policies and save report
+  shell: bash
+  run: |
+    mkdir -p build
+    vendor/bin/guard check --format=json | tee build/guard-report.json
+```
+
+An existing artifact upload step can collect the report with `if: always()`.
+Exit `2` writes the diagnostic to stderr, so the report may be empty. Check the
+step status before consuming JSON. Display filters still fail on hidden errors;
+use `--no-baseline` only for a deliberate audit of all existing violations.
+
+Sources: [workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax),
+[checkout](https://github.com/actions/checkout), and
+[setup-php](https://github.com/shivammathur/setup-php).

+# Guard in GitHub Actions
+
+Add Guard to the existing lint job after installing Composer dependencies,
+including the dev dependency `k-kinzal/guard-php`. Use a PHP version and extensions
+compatible with the project's locked dependencies. A job that already runs
+`composer lint` with `@guard` does not need another Guard step.
+
+```yaml
+- name: Check project policies
+  run: vendor/bin/guard check --format=text
+```
+
+CI checks the committed `guard.yaml` and baseline. Run `init`, `fix`, and baseline
+generation locally when requested, review their changes, and commit the result.
+Keep Guard's nonzero exit status so violations and invalid inputs fail the job.
+
+## Standalone workflow
+
+This example assumes a root Composer project with a committed lock file, Guard
+installed as a dev dependency, and a reviewed `guard.yaml`. Adapt `main`, PHP
+`8.5`, and extensions to the target project. Keep action pins consistent with
+the repository's update policy.
+
+```yaml
+name: Guard
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash
+
+jobs:
+  guard:
+    name: Check project policies
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
+      - name: Set up PHP
+        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
+        with:
+          php-version: '8.5'
+          extensions: dom
+          coverage: none
+          tools: composer:v2
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: composer install --no-interaction --prefer-dist --no-progress
+      - name: Check project policies
+        run: vendor/bin/guard check --format=text
+```
+
+## Package policies and reports
+
+For a package with its own dependencies, set `working-directory` on both the
+install and check steps, or on the job's `defaults.run`. For a root installation
+checking a package policy:
+
+```yaml
+- name: Check package policies
+  run: vendor/bin/guard check --config=packages/example/guard.yaml --format=text
+```
+
+For a JSON report in an existing job, use a permitted output directory such as
+`build/` and Bash `pipefail` to retain Guard's exit status through `tee`:
+
+```yaml
+- name: Check policies and save report
+  shell: bash
+  run: |
+    mkdir -p build
+    vendor/bin/guard check --format=json | tee build/guard-report.json
+```
+
+An existing artifact upload step can collect the report with `if: always()`.
+Exit `2` writes the diagnostic to stderr, so the report may be empty. Check the
+step status before consuming JSON. Display filters still fail on hidden errors;
+use `--no-baseline` only for a deliberate audit of all existing violations.
+
+Sources: [workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax),
+[checkout](https://github.com/actions/checkout), and
+[setup-php](https://github.com/shivammathur/setup-php).

Use `guard rules --query=structure` to inspect directory constraints and

Configuration findings use the rule's own `id`, such as `phpstan.level`, rather
than a `configuration.*` prefix. Inspect the target field and expected value with:

```bash
vendor/bin/guard rules --query=phpstan.level
vendor/bin/guard check --fixable
vendor/bin/guard fix --dry-run
```

## Repairs

`equals` supplies its own repair value. Other assertions need an explicit
`repair`; a compliant field is left unchanged. JSON5 and PHP-CS-Fixer PHP files
are check-only. Missing files, unsupported writes, or conflicting rules need
manual changes.

While a required configuration rule remains unsatisfied in the planned result,
no repairs are written and the action is `blocked`. Resolve that rule and preview
again. Metric, structure, and document findings do not block these writes.

A changed JSON, YAML, NEON, or TOML file is serialized again and may lose comments
or change indentation. XML preserves other nodes and comments. Review the diff
and run the affected tool after `guard fix`.

## Rule fields

- Define `id`, `file`, `select`, and `assert`. Imports merge rules by `id`, so an
  override need only specify the fields being changed.
- Use JSON Pointer for JSON, YAML, NEON, and TOML, and a single-node XPath for XML.

- Messages should name the file and field, the expected value, and the edit.
  Templates accept `{file}`, `{select}`, `{expectation}`, and `{fix}`.

```yaml
version: 1
configuration:
  - id: application.driver
    file: settings.yaml
    select: /driver
    assert: {one_of: [mysql, pgsql]}
    repair: mysql
```
